status: Window key/index and expression-directory lifetimes admitted across row, run and vector backends; result payload and row ownership remain open
contract: Each compatible sort group has a scope for partition/order keys and row indexes. Row evaluate and vector batchExprValues/valueAt receive that scope, so key expansion is admitted before construction and released after the group.
Sort workspace, partition spans, vector entry metadata, run cursor directories and merged partition references are admitted. Merged-partition references release when the generator advances or closes.

Identical-order expressions reuse the immutable sorted index directly. Prefix-order expressions admit copied metadata based on actual enumerable fields, key slices and peer-stabilization workspace; temporary expression scopes release before the next expression.
Window expression and partition result directories are admitted around evaluation. This does not yet admit every computed scalar/collection payload or the copied backend output rows.

Run indexes add run positions to the existing indexed records instead of mapping into another set of records. Order-expression lists are built once per index construction, and the default comparator order term is shared rather than allocated per comparison.

cases: Partition-key and order-key replace expansion succeeds with small values and rejects oversized values under 16 KiB for row, run and vector execution. Cleanup preserves sibling reservations.

Identical-order index reuse returns the same array with zero new reservations. Prefix ordering restores original peer order without mutating the shared full-order index; insufficient workspace rejects and releases cleanly.

Real Brotli HTTP 206/ignored-Range 200 and native local Worker R2 matrices include window partition/order expression routes, separately from WHERE/projection. Both row and owned-vector scanners use direct-value WHERE selection so oversized key tests reach key evaluation.

Pure adaptive peer-index exact-boundary and fallback tests remain at the kernel level. Whole-window/task tests now include mandatory key/index storage: tiny caps reject and adequate caps preserve results and release all tracked allocations.

The previous zero/3,204-byte whole-window assertions were not valid whole-path bounds because they omitted key/index storage. Tests now explicitly distinguish prepared-kernel workspace from complete backend index construction.

limits: Backend copied rows, new result properties, computed scalar/collection payloads and several internal kernel workspaces still require ownership integration.
Sort-group planning metadata, delegated task outputs, final collection and checkpoint encoding/state parsing remain separate open requirements.
Identical-order index reuse and removal of extra run-index copies are structural allocation reductions; no timing speedup or total Worker heap cap is claimed.
The complete acceptance matrix and final release gates remain open.
